doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Opening at the San Diego Jazz Party; Chicago roots
summary: Monk Rowe introduces Ray Sherman, who says he is really a Chicagoan who moved west at 16.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: We are filming at the San Diego Jazz Party. My name is Monk Rowe and we’re here for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. And I am very pleased to welcome jazz pianist Ray Sherman. And I want to call you a plumbing thing — but like a fixture on the west coast, all right? You’ve been here for most of your life.

Yeah, I’m really a Chicagoan. Shall I plug my next album? It’s called “Piano Chicago Style.” But I really, as I was going through that and putting it together I really started, I’m a Chicagoan really. I moved out here, I was 16 years old. But I think your formative years, where you grow up—
Well Chicago was a pretty darn good place to have some formative years, wasn’t it?
